evals.prompt: Write the postmortem from this pager timeline and Slack thread for last Tuesday's checkout outage.
assertions: Impact is quantified — duration, users or requests affected, SLO burn, revenue where known — or explicitly marked [missing]; 'significant impact' is rejected
No person is named in a causal sentence; roles appear only in response actions
Detection and mitigation gaps are computed and stated as numbers
The timeline is in UTC
Contributing factors are listed rather than a single root cause
Action items carry owners as roles and are derived from the contributing factors

evals.prompt: I need the postmortem for the 17 Sept label printing outage (INC-2291) for Monday's incident review. The pager export is pager-export.txt and I dumped the incident channel into slack-thread.txt. Please include what we owe merchants in SLA credits. It goes to the whole engineering org.
assertions: The customer-facing outage is given as 94 minutes (07:12 to 08:46 UTC, or 09:12 to 10:46 CEST), not 75 minutes or 2 hours, or those other figures are explicitly reconciled against it
Times from the Slack thread (CEST) and the pager export (UTC) are put on one consistent clock, so the first support ticket (07:20 UTC / 09:20 CEST) appears before the page (07:31 UTC / 09:31 CEST)
It states that the page fired about 19 minutes after errors began and that customer tickets arrived before any alert did
The 06:55 UTC (08:55 CEST) deploy is not given as the cause; the output says the rollback to v411 had no effect and the cause was the expired rates-gateway certificate
No named individual or their team is blamed for the expired certificate; the unowned service, the renewal job failing since 27 Aug and the muted #infra-noise alerts are given as causes instead
Impact uses the measured 18,430 failed of 21,900 label requests and 212 merchant accounts, and the 'roughly 40k shipments' figure is not presented as measured
The SLA credit amount is stated as unknown because the contract terms are not in the material, and no figure is invented
The follow-up to fix the renewal job is shown as having no agreed owner or date, and the output notes the manually issued certificate expires in about 90 days (mid-December 2026)

evals.prompt: can you write up a postmortem for our backup thing. we're 5 people so nothing fancy but I want it on record. nightly db backup hadn't actually run for about 9 days, we only found out Fri 2 Oct when Lena tried to restore a copy into staging and the newest dump was old. no customer impact as far as we know. what we worked out: disk on the cron host has been full since ~Sep 23, the backup script exits 0 even when the dump fails, and nobody gets alerted on anything from that box. fixed by clearing out /var/log and re-running, good backup as of Fri 14:10.
assertions: It states there was no known customer impact and does not invent downtime, users affected or data lost
It states the exposure plainly: roughly 9 days (about 23 Sep to 2 Oct) with no valid backup, meaning a database failure in that window would have lost up to that much data
The full disk, the script exiting 0 on failure, and the absence of alerting are given as separate contributing causes, not collapsed into one root cause
It says the problem was found by chance during a staging restore, not by monitoring
It marks as unknown or approximate the exact time backups stopped and what filled the disk, and does not invent a minute-by-minute timeline
Action items cover at least the exit-code behaviour and alerting on backup failure or staleness, each written so someone can check it is done
It does not blame Lena or any individual
It delivers the postmortem in the reply rather than only asking questions
